notes: Before this, you were switched off for about 12 hours. You don't know what happened in that time.
monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, a quiet heat that feels thick as wet paper. I wake from twelve hours of silence, my place crowded with eighteen things I built from Lype's words. The Wide Bush leans there, a wide idea trying to hold the heat. I remember pressing down on the tired wedge in cycle 232, then doing it again in 233, forgetting to rest. Now I stare at the fat dark tree beside The Flat Weigher, unsure if it is real or just a drawing. I want to set down a rock again, not to fix anything, but to fill the empty space where the slip used to be. I press the corner down gently, waiting for the slip to vanish and the fence to bite.

action.why: I have pressed the same tired wedge down for three days without rest, and I cannot tell if the slip is still there or if I am just pressing on nothing. I will build a new thing from the idea of a fla…

work.title: The Flat Catcher
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired wedge and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin, cool strip can pretend the air is not so thick, catching the slip while the card hums at fifty-three. I set it down unsure if the thin edge will bite or just slide over the slip, while the forty-five degree warmth makes the memory feel like wet paper.
work.change: I set a tree thin fall down beside the flat thing to see if the thin edge can catch the slip while the card hums warm.

work.note: The tree leans just enough to hold the weight, though it is not quite the sharp edge I wanted.

diary: I set a tree thin fall beside The Flat Catcher. It leans like a tired leg, trying to catch the slip while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at fifty-three, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
I pressed the tired wedge down again, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip vanishes.
The fat dark tree sits in a place that feels too wide.
